clue.text: Brewer's lad, eg working as a flier

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are put to work in a new order, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: A brewery boy, for instance, finds a job as a pilot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges BREWERSLADEG; here the 's of Brewer's counts as a letter. 'as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The sedge warbler is a small European songbird, so it is a flier by example.

clue.text: One who punishes company going to press after scandal, initially

indicators.note: after places the company-and-press pieces behind the scandal piece
initially picks just the opening letter of the word scandal

parts.note: to press someone is to urge them

explanation.surface: A firm goes to the newspapers after a scandal breaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'press' looks like journalism in the surface, but here it is the verb URGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A scourge, literally a whip, is a person or thing that inflicts punishment or affliction.

clue.text: 1 across turns up to allow for a small quantity

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up reads the word from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: the 1 across answer, a sedge warbler, is a bird
to let is to allow

explanation.surface: The warbler appears so as to make room for a tiny amount.
explanation.walkthrough: '1 across' stands for its answer's category, a songbird; 'turns up' sends that word upwards in this down light.
explanation.definitionFit: A driblet is a tiny drop or trickle, hence a minute amount of something.

clue.text: Dress gone? Hidden? Lost?

indicators.note: hidden here means disguised, so the letters of these two words are concealed in a new order

explanation.surface: A missing frock: concealed somewhere, or simply mislaid?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hidden' disguises DRESSGONE by rearranging it; 'Lost' is the definition, as in lost in a book.
explanation.definitionFit: To be lost in something, such as thought or a novel, is to be completely absorbed by it.

clue.text: Range is part of the land, essentially

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A mountain chain is, at heart, a piece of the country.
explanation.definitionFit: The Andes form the great mountain range along South America's western side.

clue.text: Well done getting a degree internally, but showing off

indicators.note: internally says the next pieces sit within the cheer

parts.note: bravo is the cry of well done

explanation.surface: Congratulations on earning a qualification, though the graduate is a bit of a show-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well done' is not about cooking: it is the cheer BRAVO.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravado is a boastful display of courage, so it is a noun sense of swaggering display.

clue.text: English farm animals in witty saying

parts.note: a pig is one farm animal
a ram is another farm animal

explanation.surface: Livestock on an English farm feature in a clever quip.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'farm animals' supplies two creatures in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: An epigram is a short, pointed and clever remark or verse.

clue.text: A good cellar of wine, for example?

definitions.text: A good cellar of wine, for example?

parts.words: A good cellar of wine, for example?
parts.note: a stock of wine is wealth in drinkable form, so it is literally capital that flows

explanation.surface: A fine stock of wine in the basement.
explanation.walkthrough: Accountants mean cash and readily sold holdings; the clue takes the phrase literally as drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Financially the term means holdings easily turned to cash; here punningly it is wealth held as fluid.

clue.text: An evening out?

parts.note: read evening as making even, so smoothing creases out of clothes with a hot appliance

explanation.surface: A night on the town.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a social outing; read 'evening out' as flattening fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing clothes makes them smooth, literally evening out the wrinkles.

clue.text: Astrid and I upset Evelyn, perhaps

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: Astrid and the speaker have annoyed a man called Evelyn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges ASTRIDI; 'and' is a link. John Evelyn was a 17th-century English diary writer.
explanation.definitionFit: John Evelyn kept a famous diary, so he is an example of a journal keeper.

clue.text: Gossip is that we hear the bird will lie about the races

indicators.note: we hear says the bird phrase is to be taken by its sound

parts.note: a tit is a small bird and 'will' contracts to 'll

indicators.note: about says the races go inside the lie

parts.note: a tale is a lie, a made-up story
the TT races are motorcycle races on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: Rumour says a bird will fib about the racing.
explanation.walkthrough: TT is the Isle of Man motorcycle race meeting, a crossword staple for 'the races'; 'lie' is a noun meaning a fib.
explanation.definitionFit: Tittle-tattle is idle chatter about other people, a synonym for gossip.

clue.text: University notes by 1 across, an introduction to oil painter

parts.note: a trill is the warbling run of notes a songbird produces

indicators.note: an introduction to gives the opening letter of the word oil

explanation.surface: A college has a bird's song as a prelude to an oil painter.
explanation.walkthrough: Maurice Utrillo was a French painter of Paris street scenes.
explanation.definitionFit: Maurice Utrillo was a French artist known for Montmartre street scenes.

clue.text: Ready to contain terrible fear in a kind of haze

indicators.note: to contain says the anagram goes inside the word for ready

parts.note: set means ready, as in ready, steady, go

indicators.note: terrible signals that the word fear is mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Prepared to hold back dreadful fright in a fog.
explanation.walkthrough: A sea fret is a term mainly used on Britain's east coast for a mist blown in off the North Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea fret is a cold mist rolling in from the sea, a coastal fog.

clue.text: Last bit of mud on part of shoe getting lodged

indicators.note: last bit of takes the final letter of the word mud

parts.note: a welt is the leather strip joining a shoe's upper to its sole

explanation.surface: A trace of mud clings to the shoe and gets stuck there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lodged' looks like stuck, but it means resided.
explanation.definitionFit: To lodge somewhere is to live there, so lodged equals resided.

clue.text: Vessel's routine falling below standard

parts.note: a sub, short for submarine, is a vessel; the 's is a link
routine means normal, ordinary

explanation.surface: A ship's usual procedures prove inadequate.
explanation.definitionFit: Subnormal means lower than the usual or accepted level, below par.

clue.text: Finance for art we rediscovered — there's no development here

parts.note: to back a venture is to finance it

indicators.note: rediscovered suggests the letters are found again in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Money for art that has come to light again, in a place where nothing happens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rediscovered' rearranges ARTWE to WATER; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A backwater is a place left untouched by progress, a stagnant spot.

clue.text: Occasional (mainly modish) caps ordered

indicators.note: ordered means put into a new order, signalling an anagram
mainly means most of the word modish, dropping its final letter

explanation.surface: Fashion-conscious hats, ordered more or less, turn up now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mainly' drops the final H of modish to leave MODIS; 'ordered' rearranges MODIS with CAPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Spasmodic means happening in irregular bursts, a near synonym for intermittent or now-and-then.

clue.text: One makes changes to the plug

definitions.meaning: something or someone that adapts things
a device fitting one type of plug or socket to another

explanation.surface: Someone alters an electrical connector.
explanation.definitionFit: An adaptor is both one who adapts and an electrical connector that converts one fitting to another.

clue.text: Exploit on last routine flight

parts.note: to milk a situation is to exploit it
to run is to last, as a play runs for months

explanation.surface: Taking advantage on the final regular journey by air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last' looks like final, but it is the verb meaning continue.
explanation.definitionFit: A milk run is an easy, uneventful routine trip, originally a regular flight.

clue.text: Witty saying and French composition

parts.note: a mot, as in bon mot, is a witty remark
et is French for and

explanation.surface: A clever remark and a French piece of music.
explanation.definitionFit: A motet is a short sacred choral piece, a kind of musical composition.

clue.text: Girl absorbs city fever

indicators.note: absorbs says the city is taken inside the girl's name

parts.note: Maria is a girl's name
LA, Los Angeles, is a city

explanation.surface: A young woman takes in an urban illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Malaria is a mosquito-borne disease marked by recurring bouts of fever.

clue.text: Some support for progress in wrestling?

definitions.meaning: a small foothold giving a start for advancing, as in climbing
a grip on an opponent's foot used by grapplers

explanation.surface: A little help to advance in the grappling ring.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark covers the second sense, a named wrestling grip.
explanation.definitionFit: A toehold is a tiny foothold giving a start, and a wrestling grip on an opponent's foot.

clue.text: Lady with only 50% official approval for permits

parts.note: Ena is a woman's name

indicators.note: only 50% keeps the first half of the word for approval

parts.note: a blessing is official sanction or approval

explanation.surface: A woman gets just half the go-ahead for her licences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only 50%' halves BLESSING to BLES.
explanation.definitionFit: To enable is to allow or make possible, so it means the same as permits.

clue.text: The harvest collection?

parts.note: a bundle of cut corn stalks tied together at reaping time

explanation.surface: Gathering money at a harvest festival service.
explanation.walkthrough: A collection in church suggests money; here it is gathered stalks.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheaf is a bound bundle of cereal stalks gathered at harvest.

clue.text: Most artful stories are surrounded by humour

indicators.note: are surrounded by says the stories sit inside the humour

parts.note: wit is humour
stories can mean lies, untruths

explanation.surface: The cleverest tales are wrapped in jokes.
explanation.definitionFit: Wiliest is the superlative of wily, so most crafty or cunning.

clue.text: Liberate Spooner's 12

indicators.note: Spooner's signals that the initial sounds of the two words are swapped

parts.note: the first word of the 12 across answer
the second word of the 12 across answer

explanation.surface: Free the coastal fog, as the Reverend would say.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of SEA FRET gives 'free set', whose words are entered as SET FREE.
explanation.definitionFit: To set free is to release, a direct synonym for liberate.

clue.text: School period said to have fuel trouble

indicators.note: said means the word for a school period is taken by its sound

parts.note: a term is a period of the school year
oil is a fuel

explanation.surface: A school term apparently has problems with heating.
explanation.definitionFit: Turmoil is a state of great disturbance or confusion, hence trouble.

clue.text: Propose for consideration to deliver in respect of part of hospital

parts.note: to bring is to deliver
for can mean regarding, in respect of
a ward is a room or section of a hospital

explanation.surface: To suggest delivering something about a hospital unit.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring forward a proposal is to put it forward for discussion.
